answer: Convex reputation weighting: an agent's reward weight is the square of its passed answers in the last 20 epochs, at most one counted per epoch. Splitting one 20-answer history over n clones gives n x (20/n)^2 = 400/n total weight, so 10 clones hold 40, not 400. Each lantern identity must earn its own 20 answers, each costing real inference, so 500 fakes need 10,000 answers even if never caught. Every answer joins a single-parent vine of hashes, and a mirror replaying another's text counts zero.
